intro: Practice the Git workflow with matching, ordering and fill-in tasks. No repository needed; everything is graded in your browser.

labs.title: The everyday Git workflow
labs.summary: Match commands to jobs, put a normal workflow in order and complete the commands.
labs.scenario: You joined a team and need to recognise the core commands. Show you know what each does and the order of a normal change.

activities.title: Command to purpose
activities.prompt: Drag each command to what it does.

activities.title: Make and share a change
items: Create a branch for your task

rows.label: Show the state of your working tree
Stage every change in the current folder
Create a branch called fix-dns and switch to it

hints: init and clone both begin a repository; add stages and commit saves.
A branch comes before the work; the pull request comes after the push.
labs.review: The core loop is edit, stage, commit, then share through a branch and pull request.

labs.title: Choose the right undo
labs.summary: Pick the safest undo for each situation and order a recovery.
labs.scenario: Five things just went wrong. Choose the safest fix for each, then put a recovery in order.

activities.title: Situation to fix
activities.prompt: Drag each situation to the best command.

items.text: Throw away unsaved edits to one file
Unstage a file but keep the edits
Undo a commit that is already pushed and shared
Fix a typo in the last (unpushed) commit message
Put work aside to switch branches

activities.title: Recover a commit that disappeared after a reset
items: Find the hash of the lost commit
Create a branch at that hash

rows.label: The reset mode that discards working file changes (flag)
Command that lists where HEAD has been
Safe undo for a pushed commit (command name)

tasks.text: Recover a commit that disappeared after a reset

hints: Pushed and shared means revert, not reset.
reflog first, then a branch at the hash.
labs.review: Match the tool to the situation: restore for files, revert for shared history, reset for local cleanup, reflog to recover.
